title: Beyond Endpoint Gains: A Weight-Delta Audit of Medical Specialization
abstract: arXiv:2608.20768v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Specialist language models are usually understood through endpoint gains: the generalist scores lower, the specialist scores higher, and the difference is treated as evidence of specialization. This leaves the released update itself largely unexamined. We propose a paired weight-delta path audit and apply it to two public, aligned generalist-to-medical-specialist checkpoint pairs: Gemma-3-4B-IT to MedGemma-4B-IT and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to HuatuoGPT-o1-7B. In both pairs, the full decoder-side update strongly reconstructs measured medical benchmark movement (0.974 and 1.183 endpoint-normalized retention), making each decoder delta an appropriate substrate for the audit. Yet the movement is not cleanly localized. MLP is the strongest broad component family in both pairs, but mixed off-domain movements, 10-seed matched controls, and endpoint-anchored rollbacks prevent a unique coarse-family explanation. translated_title: 超越端点增益：医学专业化的权重增量审计

tldr: 本文提出了一种权重增量路径审计方法，用于分析医学专业化模型更新，发现解码器侧更新能重建基准移动，但专业化效应并非局限于单一组件家族。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a weight-delta path audit method to analyze medical specialization model updates, finding that decoder-side updates reconstruct benchmark movement, but specialization effects are not localized to a single component family.
